nodes.label: ADR 0001: MapLibre GL with a WebGL2-required vector basemap
nodes.rationale: Chosen because funworldmap is fully client-side and static-hosted with no backend, and needs crisp rendering at any zoom, runtime-themeable styling, per-feature hit-testing, smooth camera animation, and a permissively-licensed stack with no account or API key. Status Accepted, 2026-05-30.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0001: maplibre gl with a webgl2-required vector basemap

nodes.label: MapLibre GL JS (rendering choice)
nodes.rationale: Open-source fork of Mapbox GL JS. Picked over Mapbox GL JS (proprietary license, access token, billing) and Leaflet + raster tiles (blurs on zoom, no runtime theming, weaker vector interaction). Cost: ships as a single non-tree-shakeable ~275 KB gzip bundle, the dominant bundle cost.

nodes.label: OpenFreeMap Positron vector basemap
nodes.rationale: Free, key-free vector basemap. Depends on the OpenFreeMap CDN; if tiles fail, bundled country polygons still render and BasemapBanner surfaces the degradation.

nodes.label: WebGL fallback / "WebGL Not Available" overlay
nodes.rationale: maplibregl.Map prefers WebGL2, falls back to WebGL1 (verified against maplibre-gl 5.23; v4 was WebGL2-only), and throws only when no WebGL context exists at all. useMapInstance catches the throw so WorldMap.tsx renders a graceful unsupported message instead of a blank canvas.

nodes.label: ADR 0002: URL hash as the single source of truth for selection and routing
nodes.rationale: Deep-linkable selection (#FRA), shareable game routes (#game/<mode>), and working back/forward were required on a static host with no server-side routing. Rejected React state/context only (no deep links) and a router library like React Router (path-oriented, heavier than needed — YAGNI). Status Accepted, 2026-05-30.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0002: url hash as the single source of truth for selection and routing

nodes.label: hashState module (parseHash / writeHash)
nodes.rationale: Parsing and serialization live in one module (src/lib/hashState.ts) because routing is hand-rolled string parsing rather than a router library — minimal surface, but the rules must stay authoritative in one place.

nodes.label: useSelectedCountry re-derivation from hash
nodes.rationale: Components hold no independent selection state; the hook re-derives from the hash on every hashchange and applies deselection itself, because deselect clears the hash via history.replaceState, which fires no hashchange event.

nodes.label: ADR 0003: Single useGameSession reducer with a discriminated-union action set
nodes.rationale: Game state (lives, score, streak, round index, outcomes) must stay consistent across modes — e.g. score and reveal animation must always agree. Rejected multiple useState values (state scatters, invariants drift) and a state-machine library like XState (dependency and conceptual overhead disproportionate to this state size). Recorded 2026-05-30 during the retention-v1 build.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0003: single usegamesession reducer with a discriminated-union action set

nodes.label: Discriminated-union action set (start/attempt/advance/overrideRound/endGame/finishFree/finalize/restart)
nodes.rationale: Atomic multi-effect transitions become expressible — restart collapses endGame+start into one dispatch to avoid an intermediate idle render (the fix for bug #32, the game-over → hash-mode-switch race).

nodes.label: GameMode contract
nodes.rationale: Modes plug into the pure reducer through a contract; orchestration (timers, reveal effects, persistence) lives outside the reducer in GameController and hooks, which keeps the reducer pure but spreads timing logic across the controller/hook layer.

nodes.label: Architecture Decision Records README
nodes.rationale: ADRs are for load-bearing decisions that need to be discoverable as decisions; anything that can live as a paragraph in docs/systems/ should live there instead.

nodes.label: ADR filing convention
nodes.rationale: Filename NNNN-short-kebab-slug.md, next available number wins. Required sections: Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives, Status (Proposed/Accepted/Superseded by NNNN/Deprecated), Date. ADRs 0001–0003 are a deliberate one-time exception to the no-historical-backfill guidance, for discoverability in a showcase repo; 0004 onward follow the guidance.

nodes.label: ADR superseding policy
nodes.rationale: A superseded ADR is kept in place for historical continuity; the newer ADR names the superseded number and the old record's Status becomes 'Superseded by NNNN'. History is annotated, never deleted or reused.

nodes.label: funworldmap Documentation Index
nodes.rationale: Prescribes a reading order for developers: purpose first, then system overview for architecture context, then individual systems as needed.

nodes.label: Bandwidth watch (GitHub Pages ~100 GB/month cap)
nodes.rationale: Flag when monthly cumulative approaches 70 GB (daily uniques × ~680 KB gzipped page weight + tiles). Response ladder: rate-limit advisory banner (extend the BasemapBanner pattern), then migrate to Cloudflare Pages for free unlimited bandwidth — custom-domain DNS can be re-pointed without rebuilding the bundle.

nodes.label: Data freshness cadence table
nodes.rationale: REST Countries quarterly review (currently unowned — file a data-freshness issue when due), CIA World Factbook archive frozen Jan 2026 (read-only), world-atlas on npm upstream release, flags refreshed per update-data run. If a refresh diff exceeds ~10% of lines, bisect by source before committing.

nodes.label: Basemap degradation response
nodes.rationale: probeBasemap runs on map init with a 3s timeout; BasemapBanner surfaces the notice while country polygons stay interactive. Confirm by hitting tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/positron directly. Recovery is a user-initiated reload via the banner Retry action — there is deliberately no automated failover to a secondary provider yet.

nodes.label: Incident response for a broken deploy
nodes.rationale: Revert-first: git revert the bad SHA on main and let the deploy workflow republish the prior good state, then post-mortem in an issue. A forward fix is tracked separately from the revert so recovery is never blocked on diagnosis.
nodes.norm_label: incident response for a broken deploy

nodes.label: Deploy workflow (.github/workflows/deploy.yml)
nodes.rationale: Builds on every push to main and publishes via actions/deploy-pages; no manual deploy step. Secrets VITE_SENTRY_DSN, VITE_CF_WA_TOKEN, VITE_ANALYTICS_ENDPOINT are all optional — each feature is env-gated and no-ops when unset. The orphan 'data' branch that held the daily content index is obsolete and may be deleted.

nodes.label: funworldmap Purpose
nodes.rationale: Identity confirmed 2026-08-03 with PRODUCT.md as the authoritative product record: earlier versions framed funworldmap reference-first, but the games shipped and became the product's center. Success is measured in craft — a polished public artifact demonstrating engineering and design quality; visitor counts are secondary.

nodes.label: Country Pinning mode
nodes.rationale: Identify a country by clicking its polygon. Three lives, unlimited rounds, distance-weighted score, running streak on correct guesses.

nodes.label: City Guessing mode
nodes.rationale: Locate a named city by clicking anywhere on the map. 10 rounds, scored by distance from the true centroid; ocean clicks are valid because the guess is spatial, not a menu choice.

nodes.label: Principle: Play Is the Front Door
nodes.rationale: The games are the primary reason to visit; reference depth serves the play and the curious moment after a round, not the other way around. The core loop is game → curiosity → lookup: a missed country is one click from its facts.
nodes.norm_label: principle: play is the front door

nodes.label: Principle: The Real Map Is the Game Board
nodes.rationale: Geography games usually happen on abstract cards or toy maps; funworldmap puts play on real country polygons with satellite imagery and terrain. Smooth fly-to animations maintain spatial context so the user never feels lost, and play never retreats to abstract quiz UI.
nodes.norm_label: principle: the real map is the game board

nodes.label: Principle: Search First
nodes.rationale: Search is the keyboard-driven complement to the map's visual navigation — fuzzy matching forgives typos, and selecting a result flies the map and opens the panel.

nodes.label: Principle: No Barriers
nodes.rationale: No application backend, no API keys, no accounts; everything ships as static files deployable to any CDN. The only server-side piece is an optional free-tier analytics Worker, and runtime network use is limited to map tiles plus optional cookieless analytics and error reporting.

nodes.label: Principle: Accessible to Everyone (with the pointer-only games carve-out)
nodes.rationale: Reference flows (map, search, panels, compare) are keyboard navigable end to end, screen-reader compatible, reduced-motion respecting, WCAG AA. The games are deliberately pointer-only (owner scope decision 2026-08-04) because guessing means physically finding the place on the globe; a spatial keyboard cursor may come later, typed guessing never will.
nodes.norm_label: principle: accessible to everyone (with the pointer-only games carve-out)

nodes.label: Scope: the canonical 195 sovereign states
nodes.rationale: 193 UN members plus the Vatican and Palestine (observer states); partially-recognized or contested territories are out of scope. Together with current-boundaries-only and no-news this is pragmatism rather than doctrine — open to revisit as of 2026-08-03, but any change starts with an explicit product decision and its own spec. The GIS exclusion stands.

nodes.label: Roadmap — Deferred Work
nodes.rationale: Explicitly not a product backlog — a parking lot for ideas scoped out during brainstorming, each citing the spec that deferred it so the rationale stays recoverable. Items are only added when a spec intentionally defers them, never for unimplemented ideas nobody proposed.

nodes.label: Flaky-on-free-CI specs (need GPU runner)
nodes.rationale: Ten specs in the chromium project's testIgnore flake on GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest because cold-WebGL on SwiftShader/llvmpipe takes 30–90s for what is near-instant locally, so waitForMapLoaded and animation-state waits time out. PR #36 mitigations (Mesa/llvmpipe, new headless mode, 4-way sharding, 30s BASEMAP_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS, fast-fail watchdog) reduced but did not eliminate them. Skip list: label-contrast, header-play-reopens-launcher, panel-focus, accessibility, axe-snapshot, reveal-animation, search, game-country-pinning, theme-and-responsive, source-tooltip-edge.

nodes.label: Self-hosted GPU runner (deferred)
nodes.rationale: The single chromium project runs --use-gl=angle --use-angle=default, which falls back to software rendering on shared Ubuntu runners with no real GPU. A real-GPU self-hosted runner is the prerequisite for putting the CI-skipped specs back into CI.

nodes.label: Theme bootstrap timing failure on mobile-webkit
nodes.rationale: All three theme-and-responsive.spec.ts failures are mobile-webkit only. Hypothesis: the inline bootstrap script in index.html reads localStorage 'funworldmap-theme' and matchMedia before React mounts, but WebKit may apply Playwright's colorScheme fixture AFTER the bootstrap runs, reversing the order the spec assumes. Acceptance: 10/10 on --project=mobile-webkit --repeat-each=10.
nodes.norm_label: theme bootstrap timing failure on mobile-webkit

nodes.label: Mobile click-tolerance failures (clickTolerance: 8)
nodes.rationale: mobile-tap.spec.ts 5px finger-roll and 12px drag cases fail on mobile-chromium and desktop-firefox-touch. Hypothesis: the tap-tolerance calculation in useMapInstance.ts may be viewport-blind or mis-handle devicePixelRatio, so 5–12px movements scale differently under mobile emulation — possibly a real bug rather than a flake.

nodes.label: Map loading failure on desktop-firefox-touch
nodes.rationale: mobile-smoke.spec.ts never sees data-map-loaded on Firefox only. Firefox uses a different WebGL2 driver stack (no ANGLE on Linux headless), so the GL context may not initialize at all — classified as a real rendering blocker, not a flake, and may need a dedicated Firefox code path.

nodes.label: Lazy Sentry (deferred)
nodes.rationale: The static `import * as Sentry from '@sentry/react'` in main.tsx bundles Sentry regardless of whether a DSN is set; moving to a dynamic import() inside initSentry would let a DSN-less build drop the library entirely.

nodes.label: Bundle-size budgets in CI (done, PR #50)
nodes.rationale: Struck through as Done 2026-05-14: scripts/bundle-budget/check.ts enforces budgets.json via npm run bundle:budget in CI. Motivated by the 2026-04-19 assessment, where the <700 KB target drifted silently with Sentry + cities.json.

nodes.label: WCAG 2.1 Level AA baseline
nodes.rationale: Treated as a per-component requirement from the start rather than a final-phase add-on. Normal text 4.5:1, large text 3:1, non-text controls and focus indicators 3:1; no information conveyed by color alone (selection changes color AND border, hover changes opacity AND cursor).

nodes.label: Honest limitation: canvas polygons cannot take keyboard focus
nodes.rationale: A WebGL2 canvas is opaque to screen readers and cannot expose individual polygons to the accessibility tree, so direct polygon selection needs a pointer. Rather than fake it, the docs state the limitation and route keyboard users through search as equivalent functionality via a different interaction path.
nodes.norm_label: honest limitation: canvas polygons cannot take keyboard focus

nodes.label: Tab order and skip links
nodes.rationale: Skip links → Search input → Play button → Satellite toggle → Theme toggle → Map container → Country panel. Source 'i' buttons are deliberately outside the Tab order (tabIndex=-1) so blur-out closes them cleanly; the compare panel's SourceMarker links are ordinary Tab stops labelled 'Source: <name>'.

nodes.label: ARIA live region announcements
nodes.rationale: aria-live="polite" announces 'France selected', '5 results for Fra', and panel open/close — changes that are visually obvious but otherwise invisible to assistive technology.

nodes.label: role="application" on the map container
nodes.rationale: Deliberately tells screen readers to pass all keystrokes to the page instead of intercepting them for quick-nav, because arrow keys pan and +/- zoom. The aria-description explicitly directs screen reader users to search for country selection, and normal navigation resumes on tab-out.

nodes.label: prefers-reduced-motion handling
nodes.rationale: flyTo uses duration: 0, CSS transitions are disabled, panel slide is instant, hover scale removed. The application checks the preference directly — MapLibre's built-in `essential` flag is deliberately not used.

nodes.label: Panel focus management
nodes.rationale: On open, focus moves first to the panel heading so screen readers announce the country name, then settles on the close button once the ~300ms slide completes. On close, focus returns to search if the country came from search, or the map container if it was clicked.

nodes.label: 44x44px touch-target floor
nodes.rationale: Exceeds WCAG 2.1 AA, aligning with WCAG 2.5.5 AAA and Material Design; 48x48 preferred, with spacing between adjacent targets to prevent mis-taps.

nodes.label: Automated axe-core auditing
nodes.rationale: Runs inside the Playwright suite catching missing labels, insufficient contrast, invalid ARIA, missing alt text, and keyboard traps. Target is zero violations on every run.

nodes.label: Analytics System
nodes.rationale: Two complementary layers, both on Cloudflare free tiers at $0/month for realistic v1 traffic.

nodes.label: Layer 1 — Cloudflare Web Analytics (passive)
nodes.rationale: Page views, IP-hashed uniques (24h TTL), referrers, country stats, Core Web Vitals. No cookies, no PII. Requires Cloudflare fronting the origin; the site token lands in the VITE_CF_WA_TOKEN GitHub secret used by deploy.yml. Custom events are impossible here — the CF WA free tier does not support them, which is why Layer 2 exists.

nodes.label: Layer 2 — Cloudflare Worker + Analytics Engine (custom events)
nodes.rationale: Client POSTs to a Worker at funworldmap.com/api/event; the Worker validates and writes typed columns to Analytics Engine, queried via CF GraphQL or the dashboard. Free-tier ceilings: Workers 100,000 req/day, Analytics Engine 10,000,000 writes/month.
nodes.norm_label: layer 2 — cloudflare worker + analytics engine (custom events)

nodes.label: track(name, props) client wrapper
nodes.rationale: Prefers navigator.sendBeacon (fire-and-forget, reliable on unload) with fetch keepalive fallback. No-ops on navigator.doNotTrack === '1', when window.__PLAYWRIGHT__ is set (a unit-test seam capturing to window.__testAnalytics), and when VITE_ANALYTICS_ENDPOINT is empty — so dev and CI e2e builds send nothing.

nodes.label: Analytics Engine column schema (indexes/blobs/doubles)
nodes.rationale: Analytics Engine stores positional arrays, so position IS the schema in SQL (blob1, blob2, …). The Worker pins a canonical ordering: index1/blob1 event name, blob2 props.mode, blob3 props.path; blob4–blob7 and double1–double6 are legacy daily-puzzle slots kept permanently reserved. Reordering orphans existing data.

nodes.label: Analytics schema migration policy
nodes.rationale: Append-only: new props go to the next unused blob/double slot, never inserted in the middle; removed props leave their slot empty forever and it is never reused for different semantics. New events only need a name added to KNOWN_EVENTS and EventName when their props map to existing positions.

nodes.label: Event: free_started
nodes.rationale: Props { mode: ModeId }; emitted when the hash router boots a #game/<mode> round (useHashGameRouter.ts).

nodes.label: Event: launcher_dismissed
nodes.rationale: Props { path: 'search'|'escape'|'card'|'backdrop'|'close' }; emitted when the launcher closes (Launcher.tsx / App.tsx). The path prop distinguishes intentional starts from bounces.

nodes.label: Event: header_cta_clicked
nodes.rationale: No props; emitted when the header Play button opens the launcher (Header.tsx).

nodes.label: Vite 8 with the Rolldown bundler
nodes.rationale: Dev uses native ES modules + HMR with esbuild transpilation that deliberately does NOT type-check (type errors surface in `npm run build` or the IDE). Production minifies, tree-shakes, hashes filenames, copies public/ flags, and code-splits world-atlas into an async chunk loaded after map init so the basemap paints first.

nodes.label: Tailwind CSS 4 (CSS-first config)
nodes.rationale: No tailwind.config.js — configuration lives in src/index.css with @custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *)) and @theme tokens. The @tailwindcss/vite plugin removes the need for any PostCSS configuration.

nodes.label: npm script surface
nodes.rationale: build = `tsc -b && vite build`; build:e2e adds --mode e2e to expose VITE_TEST_HOOKS; check = lint + typecheck + unit as the local gate; update-data and fetch-cities are on-demand data regeneration, never invoked by build.

nodes.label: Bundle budget enforcement
nodes.rationale: scripts/bundle-budget/check.ts enforces budgets.json via npm run bundle:budget in CI, total-with-async ceiling 820 KB gzip. Raising a budget requires measurement evidence in the PR, so the ceiling cannot drift silently the way the old <700 KB target did.

nodes.label: Cache header policy
nodes.rationale: index.html no-cache (always revalidate), hashed assets/* immutable for a year, flags/* one day since flags rarely change. Most static hosts set these automatically for hashed assets.

nodes.label: Static deployment targets
nodes.rationale: dist/ is fully self-contained, so Netlify, Vercel, GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, and S3+CloudFront are all interchangeable targets — which is what makes the bandwidth-cap migration path cheap.

nodes.label: On-demand, not build-time collection
nodes.rationale: The tool runs only when a developer calls npm run update-data and is never called by npm run build, so a failing or down upstream source can never break a build — the previously committed countries.json simply stays in place. Output is idempotent: the same source data produces identical output.

nodes.label: Collection pipeline (fetch → merge → flags → write)
nodes.rationale: Five stages: fetch REST Countries, fetch the CIA Factbook archive and map GEC→ISO via codesxref.csv, merge/enrich with per-field attribution and join-integrity validation against world-atlas, download ~195 SVG flags to public/flags/, then write src/data/countries.json with a change summary. Entry point scripts/fetch-countries.ts run via tsx, with per-source modules under scripts/sources/ and merge.ts.

nodes.label: Merge priority strategy
nodes.rationale: CIA World Factbook wins for government type (the primary reason that source exists); REST Countries wins for everything else as the most comprehensive general source. If any source is unavailable the whole run fails and writes nothing — there is deliberately no per-source fallback, so partial data can never be committed.

nodes.label: _fieldSources per-country attribution map
nodes.rationale: Every field's origin is tracked per country so the UI can render 'i' tooltips. Identifier fields (ccn3, cca2, cca3) are plain join-key strings with no source tracking, and data fields stay flat rather than wrapped in value/source objects.

nodes.label: REST Countries v3.1 source module
nodes.rationale: HTTPS GET /v3.1/all?fields=… under MPL 2.0; supplies names, codes, capitals, regions, population, area, languages, currencies, coordinates, borders, UN status, timezones.

nodes.label: CIA World Factbook archived source
nodes.rationale: The Factbook shut down in February 2026, so the CC0 factbook/factbook.json GitHub archive (last updated 2026-01-22) is used instead, read per country as raw JSON with government type at data.Government["Government type"].text. Acceptable because government types change slowly.

nodes.label: GEC/FIPS → ISO code mapping challenge
nodes.rationale: Factbook files key on GEC/FIPS two-letter codes (gm = Germany, au = Austria), not ISO, so codesxref.csv from factbook/factbook maps GEC → ISO alpha-2/alpha-3/numeric. Roughly 28 GEC entries have no ISO code (mostly uninhabited territories like Baker Island and Kingman Reef) and are skipped.

nodes.label: SVG flag bundling
nodes.rationale: Every flag is downloaded to public/flags/{cca2}.svg and committed (~2-3MB, gzips well) so nothing is fetched from a flag CDN at runtime; Vite serves them individually and only the selected country's flag loads.

nodes.label: Adding a new data source
nodes.rationale: Five steps: add a normalizing module under scripts/sources/, register it with a unique key, define merge priority for its fields, add metadata to _sources, then run update-data and review the diff. The architecture is meant to absorb Wikidata, World Bank, or UN data later.

nodes.label: Data System
nodes.rationale: All sources are bundled at build time — zero runtime API calls for country data, so the only network traffic is map tiles and optional cookieless telemetry. Every data point carries source attribution.

nodes.label: world-atlas / Natural Earth boundaries
nodes.rationale: Public-domain Natural Earth pre-processed as TopoJSON in the world-atlas npm package at 1:50m (~245KB gzipped) — chosen as the balance of detail and size. Each feature carries id = ISO 3166-1 numeric as a string and properties.name.

nodes.label: REST Countries v3.1 (country metadata source)
nodes.rationale: MPL 2.0; supplies name, codes, capital, region, population, area, languages, currencies, coordinates, borders, UN status, timezones, continents.

nodes.label: CIA World Factbook archive (government type source)
nodes.rationale: CC0 JSON archive of the shut-down Factbook, last updated 2026-01-22; supplies government type only. Its _sources lastUpdated reflects the archive date, not the collection run date.
nodes.norm_label: cia world factbook archive (government type source)

nodes.label: Bundled SVG flags
nodes.rationale: Downloaded at data-collection time and committed as static assets — no external CDN fetch at runtime. National flags are public domain in most jurisdictions.

nodes.label: Enriched per-country data model
nodes.rationale: Access is flat — country.population, not country.population.value — with source info held separately in country._fieldSources.population. Keeps ordinary reads simple while still carrying provenance.

nodes.label: _sources registry
nodes.rationale: countries.json carries a _sources metadata section mapping each source key to name, url, description, and lastUpdated; the 'i' tooltip resolves a field's _fieldSources key through this registry to get the display name and link.

nodes.label: world-atlas ↔ countries.json join on ISO 3166-1 numeric
nodes.rationale: Geometry and metadata are joined by feature.id ↔ ccn3 ("250" = France), making the numeric code the load-bearing key between the two datasets.
nodes.norm_label: world-atlas ↔ countries.json join on iso 3166-1 numeric

nodes.label: byNumeric / byCca3 bidirectional lookup maps
nodes.rationale: Two maps built at startup cover every conversion because CountryData carries both ccn3 and cca3: byNumeric serves map clicks (feature id → metadata → cca3 for the hash) and byCca3 serves hash/border-chip lookups (→ ccn3 for the map feature). No separate index maps are needed.

nodes.label: Canonical 195 filter
nodes.rationale: One allowlist in lib/canonicalCountries.ts (CANONICAL_CCA3 / CANONICAL_NUMERIC_IDS) applied in three places — useCountryData filters the raw 249 source rows, loadCountryGeojson filters the polygons (with missingCountriesPatch synthesizing ones the 50m dataset omits), useCityData filters cities by host country. Guarantees every rendered polygon carries full metadata.

nodes.label: Unmatched territories defensive fallback
nodes.rationale: Unreachable through normal map clicks because of the canonical filter, but retained: a polygon without a metadata match would still show the world-atlas properties.name plus 'Limited data available', with no flag and no crash.

nodes.label: Disputed territories stance
nodes.rationale: funworldmap takes no political positions: boundaries use Natural Earth's de facto defaults (as controlled in practice, not as claimed). Entities that are neither UN members nor observers are out of scope for v1 and not selectable, though their land may still appear in basemap imagery. Natural Earth's de jure and point-of-view variants remain a future option.

nodes.label: Coordinate-order mismatch (latlng vs center)
nodes.rationale: REST Countries stores [latitude, longitude] while MapLibre expects [longitude, latitude]; flyToCountry() owns the swap. Flagged as a critical implementation detail because getting it wrong silently puts the camera in the ocean.

nodes.label: Map Rendering System
nodes.rationale: MapLibre GL JS renders to a WebGL canvas with @vis.gl/react-maplibre providing React bindings; GPU-accelerated, vector, client-side-styled, no server-side rendering.

nodes.label: Satellite + 3D terrain basemap (default)
nodes.rationale: App boots into satellite mode. EOX Sentinel-2 Cloudless raster tiles plus an AWS Terrain Tiles DEM drive 3D relief (setTerrain, exaggeration 1.5) with camera pitch 20° (DEFAULT_PITCH, flattened to 0 under prefers-reduced-motion). Vector layers hide, borders render as a dark casing under a light line for contrast against imagery, and fill opacity drops so imagery shows through.

nodes.label: OpenFreeMap Positron vector basemap (toggle-off)
nodes.rationale: Clean minimal light vector style whose layer colors are modified programmatically in dark mode. All tile URLs are single constants in lib/mapStyles.ts, so swapping providers (MapTiler, Stadia, any MapLibre-compatible source) is a one-line change.

nodes.label: Satellite toggle (useSatelliteMode)
nodes.rationale: Reacts to the satellite flag: toggles satellite-* layer visibility, adds/removes terrain, hides/shows vector base layers, re-tints borders, adjusts fill opacity. The choice is deliberately not persisted — every fresh visit starts in satellite mode, with persistence tracked as a roadmap deferral.

nodes.label: country-labels symbol layer (satellite-only)
nodes.rationale: App-owned name points built from bundled latlng centroids, rendered in Noto Sans Bold served by the positron style's existing glyphs endpoint so no font assets ship. applyBasemapLayerVisibility's explicit rule is visible iff satellite && not playing — labels are hidden during active play so game answers don't leak.

nodes.label: Country map layers (LAYER registry)
nodes.rationale: Five core layers — country-fill (clickable/hover), country-borders-casing (satellite legibility), country-borders, country-dim (spotlight scrim), country-selected — plus hover, selection/compare highlight stacks, satellite raster, country-labels, country-compare-markers, and country-reveal-fill. The full registry of 18 ids is LAYER in src/lib/mapLayers.ts.

nodes.label: country-dim selection spotlight scrim
nodes.rationale: Dark 25% fill over every country except the selection (and both compare countries), sitting above base layers and below the hover/highlight stacks. Filter owned by useSelectionHighlight via spotlightDimFilter and matches nothing when no country is selected, so games never show it. Never hit-tested — every queryRenderedFeatures caller stays scoped to country-fill.

nodes.label: Hover / click / deselect interaction model
nodes.rationale: Hover sets feature-state { hover: true } on country-fill so the paint expression raises opacity and the cursor becomes a pointer; click extracts the feature id (ISO numeric) to drive selection; clicking empty ocean clears it. On touch there is no hover pre-feedback, tap maps directly to click, pinch/drag are native MapLibre, and there are deliberately no long-press gestures.

nodes.label: TopoJSON → GeoJSON boundary pipeline
nodes.rationale: Natural Earth → world-atlas TopoJSON (~245KB gzipped) → bundled by Vite as an async chunk → converted at runtime by topojson-client.feature() → added to MapLibre as one GeoJSON source with multiple layers.

nodes.label: Camera animations (flyTo)
nodes.rationale: Selection flies the camera with duration 1400, or duration 0 under prefers-reduced-motion — the app checks the preference itself rather than relying on MapLibre's built-in handling.

nodes.label: flyToCountry zoom derivation
nodes.rationale: zoom = clamp(11 − 1.7·log10(areaKm²), 2, 12), and never zooms out below the user's current zoom (Math.max(map.getZoom(), computed), per the 2026-05-17 country-click-preserve-zoom spec). Large countries land on the clamp floor; only countries under ~100,000 km² pull the camera in meaningfully. Also owns the [lat,lng]→[lng,lat] swap.

nodes.label: Dark mode via setPaintProperty
nodes.rationale: applyMapTheme (src/lib/mapColors.ts) overrides a fixed set of basemap layers — background, water, waterway, park, building — and recolors every symbol layer's text and halo, non-destructively with no style reload. A CSS filter on .maplibregl-canvas was rejected because it would transform overlay layers too, making country fill/border/selection colors unpredictable. Fallback: if layer ids can't be identified the basemap stays light while UI chrome darkens — functional graceful degradation.

nodes.label: WebGL requirement and fallback message
nodes.rationale: MapLibre prefers WebGL2 and falls back to WebGL1 (verified against maplibre-gl 5.23); the Map constructor throws only when no context can be created at all, which useMapInstance catches to show browser-upgrade guidance instead of a blank canvas. Rare — mainly enterprise browsers with GPU disabled or very old devices.

nodes.label: System Overview
nodes.rationale: Client-side SPA: all code, data, and assets ship as static files from a CDN and the browser does all the work. No application backend is required; the only server-side component is an optional analytics Worker.

nodes.label: Browser-side architecture (components → hooks → bundled data)
nodes.rationale: Three tiers inside one React app: view components (WorldMap/MapLibre, CountryPanel as sidebar or bottom sheet, Header with SearchBar + ThemeToggle), a hooks state layer (useMapInteractions, useCountryData, useCountrySearch, useTheme, useMediaQuery, URL-hash sync), and bundled data (countries.json, SVG flags, world-atlas TopoJSON async chunk, Fuse.js index built on load).

nodes.label: Runtime external dependencies table
nodes.rationale: EOX Sentinel-2, AWS Terrain Tiles, and OpenFreeMap are non-optional for their view but degrade gracefully; the analytics Worker and Sentry are true no-ops without their env vars. The Cloudflare Web Analytics beacon is the exception — it ships in every production build (stripped only in vite dev), so a prod build fetches it from cloudflareinsights.com regardless of VITE_CF_WA_TOKEN, which only controls whether CF attributes the hit.

nodes.label: Data flow: on page load
nodes.rationale: Eight steps ending in hash resolution. No loading indicator is shown while the TopoJSON chunk streams because the basemap already provides immediate visual content. Hash resolution is deliberately deferred until the GeoJSON source is loaded — a country cannot be selected and highlighted before then. Default view: satellite, lon 0 / lat 20 / zoom 1.8 / pitch 20°.

nodes.label: Data flow: on country click
nodes.rationale: queryRenderedFeatures → numeric feature id → ccn3 metadata lookup → convert to cca3 → flyTo (reduced-motion aware) → panel slides in with per-field source tooltips → hash updates to #FRA.

nodes.label: Data flow: on search
nodes.rationale: Typed query → Fuse.js against the prebuilt index → top 8 in a dropdown → selection flies the camera, opens the panel, updates the hash. No additional lookup is needed because metadata already rides along on the search result.

nodes.label: State management: hash as single source of truth
nodes.rationale: Every selection action — map click, search, border chip, initial load — updates the hash, and all consuming components react to the change rather than holding their own copy.
nodes.norm_label: state management: hash as single source of truth

nodes.label: Hook responsibilities table
nodes.rationale: Each hook is pinned to exactly one source of truth: useSelectedCountry to window.location.hash via byCca3, useCountryData to bundled countries.json parsed once, useCountrySearch to the startup Fuse index, useTheme to localStorage + prefers-color-scheme, useMediaQuery to matchMedia('(min-width: 1024px)').

nodes.label: Selection flow convergence
nodes.rationale: All four entry paths converge on setting the hash, and useSelectedCountry resolves cca3 → CountryData → flyToCountry. When the hash clears (ocean click, panel close, reset view) the hook returns null and the highlight clears — one path in, one path out.

nodes.label: Error handling matrix
nodes.rationale: Six named failures each degrade rather than crash: no WebGL → upgrade message; invalid hash → silently cleared, default view; basemap tiles fail → polygons still render; TopoJSON fails → 'Country data unavailable'; no metadata match → defensive 'Limited data available'; webglcontextlost → overlay plus restore attempt on webglcontextrestored.

nodes.label: Bundle size budget breakdown
nodes.rationale: maplibre-gl (~275 KB gzip) dominates and is not tree-shakeable; @sentry/react is statically imported regardless of DSN. Measured ~477 KB initial JS+CSS and ~710 KB with the async world-atlas chunk; per-component figures are estimates summing to the measured totals. CI enforces an 820 KB ceiling set 2026-05-14 at measured + 10%.

nodes.label: Game system (reducer + modes + controller)
nodes.rationale: One useGameSession reducer with the start/attempt/advance/overrideRound/endGame/finishFree/finalize/restart action set; modes plug in via the GameMode contract under src/game/modes/. GameSessionProvider supplies the context API and computed mode, GameController owns hash bootstrap, reveal effects, and telemetry.

nodes.label: Search System
nodes.rationale: One of the two primary navigation methods alongside direct map interaction, matching country names, capitals, regions, and codes.

nodes.label: Fuse.js client-side fuzzy search
nodes.rationale: ~8KB gzipped and runs entirely in the browser with no server or index service — consistent with the no-backend principle. Index built once at startup from ~195 records (negligible cost); each query is sub-millisecond against memory.

nodes.label: Weighted search index fields
nodes.rationale: Weights encode expected user intent: name.common 2.0, name.official 1.5, capital 1.0 ('Paris' → France), region and subregion 0.5 for regional browsing, cca2/cca3 0.3 for code lookups.

nodes.label: Fuzzy matching threshold 0.4
nodes.rationale: Approximate string matching tolerates typos and misspellings ('Untied Stats' → United States, 'Brasil' → Brazil), fuzzy substrings ('Fra' → France), and code hits ('UK' via cca2).

nodes.label: Query flow with 150ms debounce
nodes.rationale: Input is debounced 150ms to avoid excessive recomputation while typing; scored results are capped at 8 to keep the dropdown scannable, each showing flag, name, capital, region.

nodes.label: Search selection flow
nodes.rationale: Select (click or Enter) → country selected → flyTo → panel opens → hash updates → input clears → dropdown closes.

nodes.label: WAI-ARIA combobox pattern
nodes.rationale: role=combobox with aria-expanded, aria-controls, and aria-activedescendant on the input; role=listbox on the dropdown; role=option plus aria-selected per result. A live region announces result counts so screen reader users learn results exist without visually scanning.

nodes.label: No-results handling
nodes.rationale: Dropdown shows "No countries found for '{query}'" and the live region announces it; the user simply adjusts the query — deliberately no further recovery affordance.

nodes.label: Testing System
nodes.rationale: Playwright against the Vite preview server (build:e2e + preview) across four projects: chromium (real-GPU ANGLE), mobile-chromium, mobile-webkit, desktop-firefox-touch.

nodes.label: The canvas challenge
nodes.rationale: Because MapLibre renders everything into a WebGL2 canvas, you cannot query elements inside it with CSS selectors, assert CSS states on rendered features, or use standard Playwright locators for map features. This single constraint shapes the entire two-tier strategy.

nodes.label: Two-tier test strategy
nodes.rationale: Tier 1 keeps everything outside the canvas fast and reliable via DOM locators; Tier 2 reaches into the MapLibre API through page.evaluate for anything the DOM cannot express. Splitting them keeps the slow, GPU-dependent assertions confined to a minority of tests.

nodes.label: Tier 1 — DOM tests
nodes.rationale: data-testid attributes, standard role/text/testid locators, URL hash assertions, and map state mirrored onto the app root as data attributes (data-map-loaded after onLoad, data-selected-country when a country is selected) so canvas state becomes DOM-assertable.

nodes.label: Tier 2 — map integration tests via page.evaluate
nodes.rationale: Reads getZoom/getCenter, runs queryRenderedFeatures at a pixel, drives page.mouse.click at known country coordinates, and captures screenshots — the only way to assert camera and feature state that lives inside the canvas.
nodes.norm_label: tier 2 — map integration tests via page.evaluate

nodes.label: Test seams (__funworldmap_map / __funworldmap_game)
nodes.rationale: useMapInstance is the single producer of __funworldmap_map; GameController and GameSessionProvider both contribute methods to a shared __funworldmap_game bag. Gated behind build-time VITE_TEST_HOOKS, set only by build:e2e via .env.e2e — so production and the standard dev server never expose them. Acceptable because the site has no accounts, auth, or sensitive runtime state.

nodes.label: WebGL2 in headless browsers (ANGLE)
nodes.rationale: Chromium launches with --use-gl=angle --use-angle=default to use ANGLE over the real GPU when available, with software fallback last. The previous SwiftShader/Software-ANGLE backend was dropped 2026-05-02: it ran 5–10× slower and was the documented largest contributor to the chromium e2e flake regression.

nodes.label: Shared readiness helpers (e2e/helpers.ts)
nodes.rationale: There is deliberately no e2e/fixtures/ directory — all reusable readiness and interaction helpers live in one module (waitForAppReady, gotoAndWaitForMap, waitForCountryTilesRendered, waitForGameTestHook, waitForAnimationIdle, openLauncher/ensureLauncherDismissed, submitAndWait/finalizeGame/getSession, routeMapTiles, waitForMapLoaded, forceWebGLContextLoss) because waitForTimeout is banned and every wait must have a named explicit-state helper.

nodes.label: What runs in CI
nodes.rationale: CI runs the chromium project only, sharded 4-way; mobile/WebKit/Firefox projects are local opt-in pending a green cross-browser baseline. Ten more specs are testIgnore'd pending a self-hosted GPU runner (issue #106). Net: 13 of 40 spec files are local-only, so those areas must be run manually before merging.

nodes.label: Visual regression screenshots
nodes.rationale: Captures initial world view, zoomed-to-Europe, country-selected-with-panel, and light vs dark. Sensitive to rendering differences, so maxDiffPixels / maxDiffPixelRatio absorb antialiasing variance.

nodes.label: Accessibility testing with @axe-core/playwright
nodes.rationale: AxeBuilder({ page }).analyze() with expect(results.violations).toEqual([]) catches missing alt text, insufficient contrast, missing ARIA, and broken label associations as WCAG AA violations.

nodes.label: UI Layout System
nodes.rationale: Design philosophy: the map is the primary interface and everything else floats on top of it. Nothing competes with the map for space; everything yields to it.

nodes.label: Mobile-first responsive strategy (1024px breakpoint)
nodes.rationale: Layouts are built for small screens and progressively enhanced; the single breakpoint is 1024px (Tailwind lg:), which also switches the country panel between bottom sheet and sidebar.

nodes.label: Bottom sheet (mobile panel presentation)
nodes.rationale: Two states, peek 40vh and full 80vh, toggled by a keyboard- and pointer-accessible chevron. It overlays rather than displaces the map, so tapping the visible map above it still selects or deselects normally.

nodes.label: Sidebar (desktop panel presentation)
nodes.rationale: Slides in from the right over a full-width map with a drop shadow, fixed width, full viewport height, scrollable for countries with extensive metadata.

nodes.label: Country panel (one component, two presentations)
nodes.rationale: The same component renders as sidebar or bottom sheet, chosen by useMediaQuery; crossing the 1024px breakpoint while open transitions the presentation without closing the panel or changing the content. Primary fields (flag, names, capital caption, region badge, exception badges, prime grid) stay visible in peek; currencies, timezones, and border chips appear when expanded.

nodes.label: Header (floating pills)
nodes.rationale: A fixed, transparent, pointer-events: none container holds individually blurred pills with pointer-events: auto, so map interactions pass through the header's empty areas. Contains wordmark (desktop), search bar, Play button, satellite/map toggle (aria-pressed), theme toggle. During a game the search bar and Play button hide; while the launcher is open the header unmounts entirely.

nodes.label: Map controls and reset view
nodes.rationale: MapLibre NavigationControl plus a custom reticle 'Reset view' button that returns the camera to lon 0 / lat 20 / zoom 1.8 / pitch 20° / bearing 0 without touching selection — the open panel and URL hash are preserved (Home key does the same). On coarse pointers every control grows to TOUCH_TARGET_MIN_PX (44px) via @media (pointer: coarse) on vendor DOM — real enlargement rather than an ::after hit extension — while fine-pointer desktops keep MapLibre's stock 29px.

nodes.label: Per-field 'i' source attribution in the panel
nodes.rationale: Desktop hover or focus shows the source name and link; touch devices toggle the tooltip on tap since hover is unavailable, dismissing on an outside tap.
nodes.norm_label: per-field 'i' source attribution in the panel

nodes.label: Compare view
nodes.rationale: Entered from an open panel's Compare pill (enterComparePicking in App.tsx, available only while a country is selected), which puts search into pick-to-compare mode; a one-time hint appears after the session's second distinct country selection. On the map A is highlighted signal and B ice-mid while every other country is dimmed by country-dim; exiting via Escape or the exit control clears B and restores borders. Desktop chromium only — the mobile Playwright projects contain no compare flow.

nodes.label: COMPARE_FIELDS shared field definition
nodes.rationale: One array drives the whole view so rows always align and no field is silently dropped. Numeric fields render as paired bars scaled to max(A,B) with a delta chip whose subject is always the larger country; categorical fields collapse identical values into a centered 'Both: …' row and show an em dash for missing values. Bars are static, so reduced-motion needs no gating. Capitals live in header captions and UN-membership/independence render as exception badges, never as rows.

nodes.label: Compare border-chip column semantics
nodes.rationale: Per-column CountryBorders route through one onCompareColumnSelect(column, cca3): a chip in column A replaces A and keeps B (compareReplaceA), a chip in column B replaces B and keeps A (compareSelect), and a chip naming the other column's country is a no-op (compareChipClick in src/lib/compareMapClick.ts). Mobile repeats the same replace-that-country semantics inside one scroll container under a compact sticky header.

nodes.label: flyToComparePair camera framing
nodes.rationale: cameraForBounds + comparePanelPadding() frame both countries in the un-occluded area — desktop reserves the panel as right padding, mobile reserves the sheet as bottom padding (innerHeight × COMPARE_SHEET_FRACTION, which is why the sheet is dvh not vh). Mobile renders at pitch 0 because cameraForBounds' globe fit ignores pitch and a tilted render of a pitch-0 fit hid the pair under the sheet (fixed 2026-07-29). Known unfixed gap: wide pairs under the 110° threshold (e.g. Brazil+Nigeria) still fall below the sheet at 390px because cameraForBounds produces a degenerate center latitude under this bottom-padding ratio and does not respond linearly to padding — needs a dedicated fix, not a numeric tweak.

nodes.label: Compare shared source footer and exception markers
nodes.rationale: Compare fields are deliberately not individually source-tagged; a shared footer lists the comparison's sources and only fields whose source differs from the dominant one carry a superscript exception marker. Shipped with C4; the single panel adopts the scheme in D2.
nodes.norm_label: compare shared source footer and exception markers

nodes.label: Three-state theme system
nodes.rationale: light / dark / system with detection priority: manual localStorage choice, then prefers-color-scheme, defaulting to system. <html> gets the dark class for Tailwind's dark: variant, basemap layers darken via setPaintProperty, country layer paints adapt for contrast, and transition-colors duration-200 prevents jarring switches. The toggle cycles sun → moon → monitor with an aria-label reflecting the next state.

nodes.label: Deep linking via cca3 hash
nodes.rationale: Selecting France yields /#FRA and opening /#FRA flies and opens the panel, enabling sharing, back/forward, and bookmarking. Implemented as a hashchange listener plus an initial parse, resolving cca3 → ccn3 through the bidirectional lookup for map feature lookup.

nodes.label: Game routes on the same hash channel
nodes.rationale: writeHash produces #game/<modeId> and parseHash also tolerates a trailing /play on inbound links; country selection and game routes share one hash channel with the app dispatching on the prefix, so the hash is the single source of truth for both.
nodes.norm_label: game routes on the same hash channel

nodes.label: Browser history semantics
nodes.rationale: Each selection pushes a history entry so Back returns to the previous country, but deselection replaces the current entry rather than pushing — deliberately avoiding a blank '#' entry, at the cost that Back after deselecting leaves the page.
